evals.prompt: i'm making a Project Zomboid mod that adds custom weapons and a crafting system. right now all my code is in one big file in media/lua/server/MyMod.lua and it's getting impossible to manage. also im worried about multiplayer cuz i heard items can get duplicated. can u restructure this into proper files and make sure crafting is MP safe? i want weapons to have durability and different damage values that i can balance later without touching code. also my OnPlayerUpdate handler is causing lag spikes on my test server. heres my current mess: [paste of 200-line monolith with mixed UI, spawning, and event logic]
evals.expected_output: Restructured mod with proper shared/client/server separation, module pattern with require(), data-driven weapon config, MP-safe crafting via sendClientCommand/server-authoritative pattern, performance-optimized OnPlayerUpdate with guard clause and throttling
expectations: Code is split into shared/, client/, server/ directories with proper loading order
Weapon stats are in a data table separate from logic
Crafting uses sendClientCommand / OnClientCommand pattern for MP safety
OnPlayerUpdate includes a guard clause and throttling mechanism
Module pattern with require() and local scope is used (no global pollution)
Durability system uses a composable component pattern, not copy-paste

evals.prompt: ok so my PZ server mod has a loot distribution system for military bases but the containers are getting bloated with like 50 items each and players are complaining. also i feel like my loot balance is biased toward guns because i play a gun build myself lol. i want to design a fair loot table with diminishing returns so no single container is OP. also need sandbox options so server owners can tune the spawn rates. right now i just table.insert everything into the vanilla ProceduralDistributions. how should i redesign this?
evals.expected_output: Data-driven loot table with rolls/weight system, OnFillContainer or ProceduralDistributions pattern that avoids bloat, sandbox-options with configurable multipliers, anti-bias balancing principles applied, diminishing returns explanation
expectations: Loot tables use roll+weight pattern instead of flat table.insert
Sandbox options are defined and cached (not read in hot loops)
Anti-bias principles are applied (opportunity cost, diminishing returns)
Container bloat prevention strategy is explained
Server owners can configure spawn rates without touching code

evals.prompt: i wanna add a vehicle handling overhaul to PZ that reduces drift and makes cars feel more realistic. also need to know how to make it work in multiplayer without desync. my current approach just modifies vehicle values directly in OnTick and it's super laggy plus other players see the car teleporting around. what's the right way to do vehicle physics mods? also how does the anti-cheat interact with modified vehicle speeds?
evals.expected_output: Vehicle physics tuning via .txt scripts (not runtime modification), server-authoritative vehicle state, performance pattern for vehicle updates, anti-cheat type 2/3 compatibility guidance, centerOfMassOffset/rollInfluence/wheelFriction tuning advice
expectations: Vehicle physics changes are primarily in .txt scripts, not OnTick
Server-authoritative approach for MP vehicle sync is explained
Performance pattern avoids per-tick heavy computation
Specific vehicle parameters (mass, wheelFriction, centerOfMassOffset) are referenced
